caveats: Profiles not captured because the system is in accessibility mode 'standard' and these claim another: apple-macos-26.5-1x-light-reduced-transparency, apple-macos-26.5-1x-light-increased-contrast. macOS exposes reduce-transparency and increase-contrast as read-only environment values, so each such profile needs its own run with the corresponding System Settings toggle on (Accessibility > Display).

Profiles not captured because this display renders at 2.0x and their keys state another scale: apple-macos-26.5-1x-dark-standard, apple-macos-26.5-1x-light-standard. A profile is only captured on a display whose backingScaleFactor matches its key — a mismatched run would file 640x400-pixel fixtures under a key claiming a different scale, with no trace in the bytes.

Captured with reduce-transparency also on. That is not contamination: macOS couples the toggles (Increase Contrast force-enables Reduce Transparency, and the transparency checkbox cannot be uncleared while contrast is on — user-verified 2026-08-29), so this is the only reachable increased-contrast state and the one a real user sees.
